questions.question: In a perfectly competitive market, an individual firm is usually described as a
choices: price maker
price taker
single seller
government agency

questions.question: Which feature is most characteristic of a monopoly?
choices: Many small sellers offer identical products
Firms enter and exit with no barriers
One seller controls a market with no close substitute
Buyers set every firm's production level

questions.question: Which market structure has a few large firms whose decisions can affect one another?
choices: Perfect competition
Monopoly competition
Public ownership
Oligopoly

questions.question: A firm sells a product that is differentiated by brand but competes with many similar sellers. Which market structure is most likely?
choices: Monopolistic competition
Monopoly
Perfect competition
Bilateral monopoly

questions.question: Why can high startup costs act as a barrier to entry?
choices: They guarantee that every firm earns a profit
New firms may be unable to obtain the capital needed to compete
They prevent consumers from comparing products
They make demand perfectly elastic

questions.question: A single water utility serves a region because duplicating its pipes would be costly. This situation is often classified as
choices: perfect competition
monopolistic competition
a natural monopoly
a labor union

questions.question: Two dominant airlines match each other's fare changes. This is evidence that
choices: the market contains only price-taking firms
demand no longer affects prices
the firms have no strategic interaction
each firm's decisions may depend on competitors' responses

questions.question: Which change would most likely increase competition in a market?
choices: Reducing unnecessary legal barriers to entry
Granting one firm exclusive control of key inputs
Increasing switching costs for all customers
Banning new firms from entering

questions.question: A company lowers its price, and rival firms quickly respond with similar cuts. What concern may this create for the firms?
choices: The market becomes a monopoly immediately
Price competition can reduce each firm's profit margin
The product becomes a public good
All consumer demand disappears

questions.question: Which market outcome is most likely when a single seller faces little competition and consumers have few substitutes?
choices: The seller must accept the market price
The seller cannot earn revenue
The seller may have greater power to influence price
Consumers determine the firm's production costs

questions.question: What is a key difference between a public good and a private good?
choices: Private goods are always supplied by governments
Public goods have no production costs
Private goods are available to everyone without payment
Public goods are generally nonexcludable and nonrival

questions.question: A company owns the only local patent for a specialized medicine. The patent may create a temporary barrier because it
choices: limits other firms' legal ability to produce the same patented invention
guarantees the company unlimited demand
removes the need for safety testing
prevents consumers from seeking substitutes

questions.question: If a market's firms can enter easily when profits rise, what is likely over time?
choices: Existing firms will become permanent monopolies
New entry may increase supply and place pressure on prices and profits
Consumer demand will stop affecting output
All firms will face identical production costs

questions.question: Two companies combine and become the only sellers of a necessary local service. Which issue would regulators most likely examine?
choices: Whether the companies have attractive logos
Whether every customer buys the same amount
Whether the merger substantially reduces competition or harms consumers
Whether market demand is completely fixed

questions.question: Which measure best describes a firm's market share?
choices: Its total number of employees worldwide
Its tax rate compared with the average
Its production cost per worker
Its portion of total sales in the relevant market

questions.question: A firm in a competitive market develops a process that lowers its costs. What can happen if rivals cannot copy it immediately?
choices: The firm may earn higher profits until competition responds
The firm must raise its costs to match competitors
The market becomes a public good
Consumers lose all bargaining power

questions.question: Why do economists define the relevant product and geographic market when evaluating competition?
choices: It determines the company's advertising style
The definition affects which sellers and substitutes count as competitors
It removes the need to measure market shares
It proves every large firm is a monopoly

questions.question: A new app makes it easy for customers to compare prices across sellers. What is one likely competitive effect?
choices: It creates a legal barrier to all new firms
It guarantees equal market shares
It may reduce some sellers' ability to charge much more than rivals
It eliminates differences in product quality

questions.question: A small town has one grocery store, but residents can shop online or drive to a nearby town. Why should those alternatives be considered before calling the store a monopoly?
choices: A monopoly is defined by a store's building size
Online sales are never part of a market
A nearby competitor cannot affect local choices
Substitutes and the geographic market affect how much market power the store has

questions.question: Which statement best describes competition in an oligopoly?
choices: A few firms may compete while also anticipating each other's actions
Many firms act without considering rivals
One firm always has no influence on price
Prices are set only by consumers
